name: Polyseat 0.4.2
body:
Words, and the one place that cannot be looked up again. Nothing here changes how
a seat is built, so updating is a restart of the daemon and no more.

## The submenu is called *Host*

*Machine* was the wrong word for what is behind it. Preparing this computer,
checking for a newer Polyseat and removing it are the three things that are
about the host the seats run on rather than about a seat, and "host" is what
this project calls that everywhere else — down to `host/README.md`. It is also
the word a Moonlight client already has for the machine it streams from.

The panel inside it is *Prepare this host*, and the ids in the interface code
went with the label: a dialog titled "This host" reached through
`el("machine")` is two names for one thing, and the second one is the one
somebody greps for.

## What pacman prints after installing says less, and says where to go

It was thirty-five lines and ended at a placeholder: "open
`https://<this machine>:47800`". It now prints the address a browser can
actually open — the IPv4 address on the interface carrying the default route,
which is the one another machine on the network can reach, and the host name
only when there is no route to ask. On a line of its own with nothing after it,
because that is what makes a terminal treat it as a link.

The AMD warning and the shared library's filesystem requirement are gone from
it. The interface says both on its own, in front of the thing they are about,
and the console is the one place where nothing can be clicked and nothing can be
looked up later. `host/install.sh` and `host/prepare.sh` end the same way now
and are about half as long.

## Updating

Press the button in the interface, or:

```
curl -LO https://github.com/superuser404notfound/Polyseat/releases/latest/download/polyseat-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
sudo pacman -U polyseat-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
sudo systemctl restart polyseatd
```
